summary: the range checks of rach2/sys/mm/paging.c and rach2/sys/arch/i686/mmu.c, the page fault handler's panic for a kernel stack that ran into its guard page, and the batched release of the temporary mappings, through paging_hosttest.c, with eight faults in private copies

argv: rm -rf ${WORK}/t && mkdir -p ${WORK}/t/tests/host && cp -R rach2 ${WORK}/t/ && cp -R ${SRC}/. ${WORK}/t/ && exec ${CC:-cc} -std=c99 -D_DEFAULT_SOURCE -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=0 -DRACH2_HOSTTEST -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -g -O1 -Wno-empty-body -ffreestanding -Wno-pointer-to-int-cast -Wno-int-to-pointer-cast -U__UINTPTR_TYPE__ -D__UINTPTR_TYPE__=unsigned -U__INTPTR_TYPE__ -D__INTPTR_TYPE__=int -U__SIZE_TYPE__ -D__SIZE_TYPE__=unsigned -U__PTRDIFF_TYPE__ -D__PTRDIFF_TYPE__=int -I ${WORK}/t/rach2/sys -I ${WORK}/t/rach2/sys/arch/x86 -I ${WORK}/t/rach2/sys/arch/i686 -I ${WORK}/t/rach2/sys/lib -I ${WORK}/t/rach2/sys/proc -I utils -I krffs -I tests/host/compat -o ${WORK}/paging_hosttest tests/host/paging_hosttest.c ${WORK}/t/rach2/sys/mm/frame.c ${WORK}/t/rach2/sys/lib/kstring.c ${WORK}/t/rach2/sys/lib/kctypes.c tests/host/compat/spinlock_host.c

faults.name: rounding
faults.summary: map_mmio_typed's page count rounded up by `+ PAGE_SIZE - 1`, which wraps for a span that begins in the first page and ends in the last

lines: paging-hosttest: fail: a span from the first page into the last, whose rounding would wrap, is refused

faults.name: loop
faults.summary: the loop of premap_kernel_window bounded by `va_start + size`, which wraps below the start for a window that runs past the top

lines: paging-hosttest: fail: a window that runs past the top of the address space is refused and makes no table

faults.name: zero
faults.summary: the refusal without its exception for address 0

lines: paging-hosttest: fail: a window that starts at address zero gets its table

faults.name: guard
faults.summary: the handler without its test of the guard page, which panics as any kernel fault

lines: paging-hosttest: fail: a supervisor fault in the guard page below the running thread's kernel stack panics as that stack's overrun

faults.name: unmap-each
faults.summary: a release of a temporary mapping that unmaps its slot at once

lines: paging-hosttest: fail: a released temporary slot stays mapped and changes no kernel mapping

faults.name: stale-reuse
faults.summary: a search that gives a released slot before a sweep

lines: paging-hosttest: fail: with no slot free, a mapping sweeps every released slot with one change of kernel mappings and takes the first

faults.name: held-swept
faults.summary: a sweep that unmaps held slots too

lines: paging-hosttest: fail: a held temporary slot is not given again and survives two sweeps

faults.name: no-change
faults.summary: a sweep that changes the kernel mappings without telling the other processors

lines: paging-hosttest: fail: with no slot free, a mapping sweeps every released slot with one change of kernel mappings and takes the first
